title: Publish Homebrew Cask and Formula
notes: This task builds on the already-landed 064a08c4 ('feat(distribution): add Homebrew source contract'), which added packaging/homebrew/release.v1.json, packaging/homebrew/Casks/membrane.rb, packaging/homebrew/Formula/membrane.rb (both intentionally-unavailable, fail-closed placeholders), tests/platform/macos/homebrew.test.mjs, and a Homebrew section in docs/install.md. None of those files were modified by this task: packaging/homebrew/** already correctly encodes the fail-closed, both-architecture contract, and tests/platform/macos/homebrew.test.mjs already passes against it (re-run in commands.log to confirm it is undisturbed). docs/install.md is outside this task's allowlist and was read but not edited.

MID-TASK CORRECTION APPLIED: this task's initial reading of MBR-901 (commit 2d543114, 'ship signed and notarized macOS app/DMG') suggested deriving Cask/Formula artifacts from that task's hand-rolled packaging/macos/release-contract.json + scripts/release/macos/contract.mjs pipeline. The orchestrator corrected this mid-task: RightKit (@rightkit/release, already an apps/membrane-hub devDependency at 0.2.51, wired as `release:build:mac` -> `right-release build --platform mac` via apps/membrane-hub/right-release.config.mjs) is the real, already-integrated signing/notarization/sealing pipeline for this app. scripts/release/homebrew/generate.mjs was written (and, after the correction, was already aligned with it, since it was designed from right-release.config.mjs and RightKit's sealed-manifest shape from the outset) to derive every Cask/Formula field from exactly two real RightKit inputs: (1) a dynamic, read-only import of apps/membrane-hub/right-release.config.mjs for app name, version, and the installer artifact -> R2 key map, and (2) a real RightKit sealed release manifest (.right-release/sealed/<app>-<version>-<commit8>/mac/release-manifest.json, gitignored local build state), whose recorded per-file SHA-256 and size are independently re-verified against the bytes on disk before being trusted. The public download URL is the sealed manifest's R2 key joined with the same RIGHTAPPS_PUBLIC_DOWNLOAD_BASE constant/env-var @rightkit/release/upload-release.mjs itself uses (default https://pub-6c73208d46c245a9b4881d5e02f6b618.r2.dev) -- never an invented URL. @rightkit/release's own verifySealedRelease (tools/rightkit/packages/release/release-state.mjs) was deliberately NOT imported: it is installed only under apps/membrane-hub/node_modules (pnpm strict node_modules, no root hoist), confirmed unresolvable from a repo-root script via `node -e "require.resolve('@rightkit/release/release-state.mjs')"` (MODULE_NOT_FOUND). A minimal, local re-implementation of the same hash/size check was written instead.

DECLARED, VALIDATED GAP -- mac-x64/Intel Cask artifact: apps/membrane-hub/right-release.config.mjs declares exactly one mac installer artifact, an aarch64 .dmg (`Membrane Hub_${version}_aarch64.dmg`); there is no x86_64/Intel target anywhere in that config. resolveCaskArtifacts() in scripts/release/homebrew/generate.mjs therefore always reports mac-x64 as `{ blocked: true, reason: '...declares no x86_64/Intel mac installer target...' }` against the real config, proven by a dedicated regression test run directly against the real (not fixture) apps/membrane-hub/right-release.config.mjs, and confirmed again by the real-world `plan` sanity run in commands.log against the actual local sealed release for commit 0d5e7077 (version 0.1.5). No Intel path or hash was invented anywhere. Per this task's hard rules, renderCask()/renderFormula() only ever produce real Ruby DSL output when BOTH mac-arm64 and mac-x64 resolve to real, validated data; with only arm64 real today, both functions fall back to the exact committed placeholder text (byte-identical to the already-landed packaging/homebrew/Casks/membrane.rb and Formula/membrane.rb, asserted by test).

DECLARED, VALIDATED GAP -- Homebrew Formula (headless CLI/daemon): apps/membrane-hub/right-release.config.mjs has no targets.mac.headless (or any other) tarball target at all; RightKit only builds/signs the full Tauri Hub .app/.dmg for mac. resolveFormulaArtifacts() therefore always reports both mac-arm64 and mac-x64 as blocked with an explicit reason, for both real and fixture inputs; this is not specific to the architecture gap above, it applies before architecture is even considered. The Formula renderer's real-output code path (on_macos + Hardware::CPU.arm? branching, `service do` block for crypt-service, `bin.install` for the membrane CLI) is still implemented and unit-tested against a synthetic, clearly-fixture 'ready' input, so the generator is functionally complete and forward-ready for whenever RightKit ships a headless artifact target -- but it never claims one exists today.

Real-world validation performed (read-only, not part of the automated suite): `node scripts/release/homebrew/generate.mjs plan --commit 0d5e7077b7ef14cd9baeb1d60ef453d6b44bae30` was run against the genuine local `.right-release/sealed/membrane-hub-0.1.5-0d5e7077/mac/` output of an earlier, real `right-release build --platform mac` (gitignored local state, not produced by this task, not committed). It correctly resolved the real arm64 DMG's real SHA-256 (4759c7c2...b3bad) and real derived public URL, and correctly reported mac-x64 and both Formula architectures as blocked with the reasons above. This directory is not part of the automated `node --test` suite -- which uses only self-contained temp fixtures built with node:fs/node:crypto in tests/platform/macos/homebrew-generate.test.mjs so the suite stays hermetic on a fresh checkout without .right-release state -- but is recorded in commands.log as direct evidence the generator's real-input code path works against a genuine RightKit sealed release, not only synthetic data.

No cargo/pnpm/Tauri build, `brew`, or signing tool (codesign/notarytool/stapler/spctl) was run. No mutating git command was run. The manifest command (`node scripts/release/verify-release-plan.mjs --task MBR-904`) was not executed, per MEMBRANE-BOOK-MODE-EXECUTION-RULES.md. Status is recorded as pending_book_gate, not pass. envBlocked is true: publishing a real, both-architecture Cask/Formula still requires (a) a real x86_64/Intel mac build target and sealed release, which does not exist in apps/membrane-hub/right-release.config.mjs today, (b) a real headless CLI/daemon release target for the Formula, which also does not exist, (c) uploading the sealed installer to the public R2 bucket (`right-release upload --tier patch`), and (d) Adrian's explicit decision to publish -- none of which this task performed or was permitted to perform.
This evidence bundle and the source files above are uncommitted; the orchestrator commits with the exact MBR-904 message.
